messages:
raja: Heads up — after the kernel tweak yesterday we see a p99 spike on canary. p95 looks fine but p99 jumped ~2x around 18:23 PDT.
emily: Ugh. Was that the kernel selection change that prefers fused attention on long seqs?
raja: yep. hypothesis: fused kernel increases single-request tail due to memory/layout path for small microbatches.
alex: Interesting — our synthetic loadgen (constant qps) didn't show it. Replay does. Could be request distribution (prefixes / kv hits) causing different kernel paths.
kevin: Can you paste the profiler snippet that showed the extra memcpy? perf-bot flagged a regression ID if helpful.
perf-bot: regression detected: reg-2026-03-17-ker-23, linked logs: https://ci.internal/reg/reg-2026-03-17-ker-23
raja: Profiler excerpt (hot path):
```
Frame: fused_attn_kernel
Self: 18.3ms
Children: kv_replay_copy 9.7ms, reorder_layout 6.1ms
```
mira: kv_replay_copy — that sounds like replay rehydration hitting a slow path. Loadgen likely doesn't hit that because it uses shorter prefixes.
emily: So two hypotheses: (A) replay fidelity is exposing a real production tail because real traffic has cached KV misses/prefixes that cause layout changes; (B) replay pipeline is artificially amplifying memops.
raja: Agreed. We need to decide measurement policy: trust replay (closer to prod distribution) or trust loadgen (stable, debuggable)?
alex: I'd vote for hybrid: use sampled real-traffic replay for tail behavior + targeted synthetic microbench for isolating kernel perf. We can then attribute tail to either request shape or kernel micro-ops.
kevin: Practically, can we do a small experiment: 1) run replay on a 10% sample of canary traffic with KV cache state restored, 2) run loadgen with same sequence length and prefix mix, and 3) run a microbatch sweep (batch sizes 1..8) with fused vs fallback kernel.
mira: I can set up the sweep. Quick note: our microbatch shaping currently auto-batches up to 4 unless latency SLO triggers. If fused kernel hurts single-request p99, we might need to reduce microbatch cap for latency-sensitive routes.
emily: But that reduces throughput. We should quantify throughput loss vs p99 gain. Can we compute tradeoff curve? p99 vs throughput across microbatch sizes and kernel choices.
raja: Exactly. I proposed a delta-matrix: rows = microbatch size, cols = kernel variant, cells = {p95,p99, throughput, cost-est}. Keep it simple to start.
perf-bot: scheduled job: hybrid-bench-2001234567 queued. ETA ~45m.
alex: Also suggest instrumenting KV-cache hit histogram in replay vs prod sample. If replay is restoring stale or zeroed cache, that would overstate the rehydration cost.
kevin: Good call — add a toggle to replay infra to preserve real cache digests. Might be tricky for PII but we can anonymize keys.
mira: For the microbatch sweep, small plan:
- run per-kernel microbench with batchwidths [1,2,4,8]
- record p50/p95/p99, tail jitter (stddev of top 1%), and tokens/sec
- capture perf counters and memcpy counts
- run both synthetics and 10k-sample replay
raja: I'll take analysis after runs. If fused kernel gives better throughput but worse p99 at batch=1, we may route latency-SLO routes to fallback kernel while letting background jobs use fused.
emily: Routing by policy is fine but increases routing complexity and maintenance. Can we instead implement a quick heuristic: if estimated tail cost > X, reduce microbatch cap for that route?
alex: Heuristic will work short-term. Long-term we need kernel fix or layout path optimization.
kevin: Small practical ask — can we include RequestShape in the bench artifacts: sequence_length, kv_hit_ratio, prompt_prefix_tokens. That will let us map where the cutoff is.
mira: Will do. I'll kick off the sweep and the sampled replay now. Posting initial artifacts to #bench-results when done.
raja: Thanks. If anyone sees the prod alert again, ping me and mark it as "canary-tail-regression". We'll correlate with bench artifacts.
emily: One more: when we report p99 be explicit about measurement windows and whether it's sample-corrected. We had confusion last time where p99 was computed on a 1s sliding window vs whole-run.
raja: Good point — we'll compute run-level p99 (all samples) and a rolling p99 (1min windows) and publish both.
perf-bot: hybrid-bench-2001234567 started on runner infra-5. Logs: https://ci.internal/logs/hybrid-bench-2001234567
kevin: Awesome. If bench shows kernel is the culprit, I'll open a small PR to gate fused kernel via a feature flag per-model.
emily: Thanks team. Let's reconvene when perf-bot posts results.
